task_text: IKEA MuJoCo SVALLET work lamp (IKEA SVALLET work lamp (AA-2140039-1), unpowered steps 1-2) with two 6-DoF ViperX 300 s arms (MuJoCo Menagerie ALOHA), each with its own parallel gripper. Press the lamp shade's key down into the socket on top of the stand column until the spring jaw snaps over it, then screw the E12 bulb up into the shade's socket until it seats. Success requirements: Both retention joints are connected (shade on the stand, bulb in the shade) and, at the end, each connector is within its gates (axial gap, lateral offset and axis tilt). The stand rests on the bench (vertical contact force above 0.1 N) and is within 3 degrees of its upright start orientation. No robot contact with any lamp part at the end. The benchmark's terminal rules, the same in every IKEA MuJoCo task, come on top of these requirements. When your rows end: (1) the requirements above hold; (2) the parts are released: no robot link touches any part; (3) every part is at rest: at most 0.01 m/s and 0.05 rad/s; (4) the simulation never broke down: no non-finite state, no MuJoCo BADQACC / BADQPOS / BADQVEL warning, no contact of a part deeper than 10 mm, at any time. The grader then holds your last row for 1.0 s more and requires (1)-(4) again at its end. Mechanism: The shade's barb cams a spring jaw (a slide joint with a spring, 1200 N/m) open and it snaps back over the barb. The bulb thread (11.9 mm x 1.5 mm right-hand, convex thread pieces) advances only by turning and seats on the socket stop. Retention welds switch on with the current relative pose when the seating gates hold. The prewired cable is not built.
